The structure is **1-phenylpropene**, C₆H₅–CH=CH–CH₃: a benzene ring carrying a propenyl
side chain.
Use the two rules — every bond contains exactly **one σ**, a double bond adds **1 π**.
**σ bonds in the ring:**
six C–C links round the ring = 6
five C–H bonds (one ring position is taken by the side chain) = 5
ring total = **11 σ**
**σ bonds in the side chain:**
ring–CH = 1
CH=CH (its σ) = 1
CH–CH₃ = 1
one H on each of the two sp² carbons = 2
three H on the methyl = 3
chain total = **8 σ**
**Total σ = 11 + 8 = 19** ✓
**π bonds:**
the benzene ring has **3** (the three formal double bonds of a Kekulé structure, in reality a
delocalised sextet, but still three π bonds' worth)
the side-chain C=C has **1**
**Total π = 4** ✓
So 19 σ and 4 π.
A check on the formula: C₉H₁₀ has 9 + 10 = 19 atoms, and an acyclic molecule with 19 atoms
would have 18 σ bonds — the **ring** adds one more link, giving 19 ✓
∴ 19 σ, 4 π.
